Adamow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Adamów, Poland

Demolished. This record shows a tension worth noting: it is categorized as 'fenced and protected,' yet the source's demolished field marks it as 'yes.' Adamów's Jewish community was subordinate to the larger community in nearby Kock, documented elsewhere in this collection, likely becoming independent only in the second half of the 19th century — as late as 1924, Adamów's Jews were still being buried in Kock. In October 1942, Germans shot over 300 Jews in Adamów and deported the rest to Łuków, documented elsewhere in this collection, and then to Treblinka. In 2001, at the initiative of Rubin Rosenberg, who had emigrated from Adamów to the United States, this cemetery was fenced with a concrete wall and a Holocaust memorial erected; a stele dedicated to Rosenberg himself, who died in 2005, was later placed beside the monument.
